question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | $e$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $1$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{3\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}}{x}\,\text{d}x & =3{\int }_{1}^{e}\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{1}{u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\cdot \frac{{u}^{3/2}}{3/2}\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2\cdot {u}^{3/2}\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2({1}^{3/2}-{0}^{3/2}) \\  & =2(1-0) \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$
